key_insight: Standard visual grounding benchmarks reward literal category matching; this paper introduces scenario-based visual grounding (RSC), where targets must be inferred from roles, intentions and relations rather than explicit names, revealing a gap in model comprehension.
problem_solved: Addresses the limitation of existing grounding evaluations that let models succeed by matching prominent named categories, instead measuring the ability to infer referents from contextual roles, intentions and relational cues.
method: Introduce Referring Scenario Comprehension (RSC), a benchmark containing queries that require role-, intention- and relation-based inference rather than literal naming.
Define an evaluation protocol and metrics tailored to scenario comprehension to distinguish category-matching from true contextual reasoning.
Provide baseline experiments and analysis showing current models' failures and where scenario reasoning is required.
impact: RSC exposes weaknesses in current vision–language models and provides a targeted benchmark to drive development of models that understand roles, intentions and relations—important for robust scene understanding in robotics, assistive tech and multimodal reasoning.

paper_title: Beyond Referring Expressions: Scenario Comprehension Visual Grounding
paper_authors: Ruozhen He, Nisarg A. Shah, Qihua Dong, Zilin Xiao, Jaywon Koo
